## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2a55ea381bfeda6b6b3cba3c7520c251a6222aa0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/http-server.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/request-body.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/adapter.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/request-body-refusal.test.ts, packages/qa/http-conformance/src/adapter.ts, packages/rest/src/http-request-test-builder.ts, packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts, packages/spec/package.json, packages/spec/tsup.config.ts, pnpm-lock.yaml (the hono resolution), and hono 4.13.12's `dist/request.js`, `dist/context.js` and `dist/utils/body.js` read from the pnpm store; PR #24005's diff and its contract review `6222965551`. The changeset `.changeset/24043-http-request-body-tsdoc.md` is a prose face, judged in ②.

Net diff against the merge base `e246f0611`: 2 files, 29 insertions, 1 deletion; one commit. The five cited code files are byte-identical at the merge base, at the current `origin/main` and at the head, so one reading covers all three. No governed path (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` green); head repo is the base repo; size/s; the card's `Claim:` names this branch and the claim guards are green.

### ① Derived judgments

Each sentence the diff adds to `IHttpRequest.body`'s TSDoc (`http-server.ts:23-39`), against the standard transport on `main`.

**S1 — "Request body, parsed by its declared content type: the parsed JSON document for `application/json`, or the parsed fields of a form (`multipart/form-data`, `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`)."** Right. `readRequestBody` parses exactly three media types: `application/json` (`request-body.ts:136`, `includes` on the lowered header, so parameters and case are tolerated) and the two form types through `parseBody()` (`:153-156`); every other media type is left unread (`:162-166`). A `+json` structured-syntax suffix (`application/vnd.api+json`) is NOT parsed, so naming `application/json` alone is exact, not an under-claim. Pinned: "a valid JSON body reaches the handler parsed", "a declared JSON media type is matched case-insensitively", "a urlencoded form body reaches the handler parsed". The multipart PARSE has no CONTROL pin (only the malformed-multipart refusal is pinned); the arm is one line and reads as described.

**S2 — "`{}` when the request carries no body."** Right on the standard transport, for the route seam and the fallback seam, both of which build the request through `runHandler`: declared JSON that is blank or whitespace is `{}` (`:145`); a request whose framing headers declare no body is `{}` whatever it declares (`declaresBody`, `:127-131`, `:164-166`). Pinned: "an empty or whitespace-only JSON body is `{}`", "a request with no body is `{}`, whatever it declares", "CONTROL over the wire: a POST with no body is `{}`". Against the other producers: the conformance `NodeHttpServer` starts from `body = {}` (`qa/http-conformance/src/adapter.ts:381`), so a no-body request is `{}` there too; the rest test builder leaves `body` ABSENT unless a fixture passes one (`http-request-test-builder.ts:77-78`, `:131-139`) — a test-layer file that tsup never emits (`:6-8`), whose header records absence as "the fixture supplied none". The standard transport's own middleware seam hands `body: undefined` on every request (`adapter.ts:1487`), but the contract already says so in its own words: the `Middleware` TSDoc (`http-server.ts:144`, "`req.body` is NOT populated") and the fallback TSDoc (`:395-398`) scope the `{}` sentence to route and fallback handlers. What the sentence leaves unexplained is the `?` on the member next to prose that names `{}`: the type permits an absence the prose never describes. A residual carried to ③ (Q1), not a contradiction.

**S3 — "Reading it may REFUSE: an implementation that cannot parse the body, or that does not read the body's media type, throws from the read rather than hand over an invented value."** Right as permission, by its lead. The clause after the colon defines what a refusal is, and its three arms match the code: an unreadable or malformed declared-JSON body (`:142-149`), a form that does not parse (`:157-158`), and a declared body in a media type the transport does not read (`:164-165`). I read it as the dev does (acceptance note): MAY, with the standard transport named in S4 as the one that does. The declarative mood of "an implementation that cannot parse the body … throws" can also be read as a norm for every implementation, and under that reading the conformance `NodeHttpServer` (`catch { body = {}; }`, `:387`) is non-compliant. That ambiguity is not a defect in this sentence; it is why the out-of-scope finding is a card (③).

**S4 — "The standard transport (`@objectstack/plugin-hono-server`) does, and answers the request itself with 400 `INVALID_REQUEST`, replacing whatever the handler wrote;"** Right. The `body` getter records the refusal and throws (`adapter.ts:728-734`). After the handler settles, `if (refusedBodyRead)` returns `c.json(envelope.body, envelope.status)` BEFORE `outcome.response ?? capturedResponse` is consulted (`:880-887` against `:893`), so a `res.json`, a `res.send` and a `res.write` stream the handler produced are all discarded, and the explicit status argument overrides any `res.status()` the handler set (hono 4.13.12 `context.js` `#newResponse`: a numeric argument wins over the context status). `RequestBodyRefusal` carries `status = 400` and `code = 'INVALID_REQUEST'` (`request-body.ts:86-94`), the two conditions `declaredEnvelopeForThrow` requires (`adapter.ts:341-348`). Pinned: the query door's own catch answers 500 and the wire shows 400 (steps 2, 3, 4 and the socket case); "a fallback that reads the body is refused like a route". One nuance, non-blocking: a response HEADER the handler set through `res.header()` lives on the Hono context (`c.header` writes `#preparedHeaders`) and rides onto the 400; the body and the status are replaced, a header is not. "Whatever the handler wrote" reads as its answer, which is what the pins measure.

**S5 — "so a handler must not catch the refusal and carry on, because anything it does after the catch acts on a request that has already been refused."** Right. The refusal is recorded at the moment of the read (`:730`), before the throw, so the adapter's answer is decided by the time any catch runs; what survives a catch is the handler's side effects, never its answer. The card's phrase "would write after a 400" was the imprecise form; the TSDoc states the measured one (the dev's Q2). No in-repo consumer catches and carries on: the dispatcher bridge reads `req.body` unguarded (`dispatcher-plugin.ts:303`) so the throw escapes to `runHandler`, and PR #24005's review (residual 8) found no catching domain.

**S6 — "A handler that needs the raw bytes (a file upload, a media type not listed above) reads {@link rawBody} and never reads `body`."** Right, and "never reads `body`" is a real constraint for the case that matters, not advice overstated. For a media type not listed above with a declared body: nothing is read before the handler (`:162-166`), `rawBody()` reads `c.req.arrayBuffer()` from the untouched stream (`adapter.ts:741-744`), and ANY read of `body` — inside a `try` or not — is a recorded refusal that dooms the answer to 400 (S4). Pinned by the three byte-door CONTROL rows (`text/plain`, `application/octet-stream`, and a JSON-with-comments file sent as `application/json`). For the listed media types the sentence is advice: the parse runs before the handler whether or not `body` is read (`:701`), and reading `body` consumes nothing `rawBody()` needs, because Hono's body cache serves both — `text()` then `arrayBuffer()` round-trips the UTF-8 bytes (hono 4.13.12 `request.js` `#cachedBody`; the JSON-with-comments pin is exactly this path). So the wording does not overclaim. What is imprecise is the parenthetical's "a file upload": a `multipart/form-data` upload IS a form that `body` parses (S1), and on the standard transport its `rawBody()` is NOT the wire bytes — `parseBody()` caches `formData` (`utils/body.js` → `parseFormData` → `request.formData()`), and `arrayBuffer()` afterwards is `new Response(formData).arrayBuffer()`, a re-serialisation with a fresh boundary. That shape predates PR #24005 (the old adapter called `parseBody()` on every non-JSON media type), is unchanged by this diff, and is not pinned either way. A reader who takes "a file upload" to mean multipart is pointed at `rawBody()` for bytes it does not get. Wording residual: "a raw upload (a PUT of the file's own media type)" names the case the transport's module note names (`request-body.ts:49-60`, the storage presign). Non-blocking here; the multipart `rawBody()` shape is escalated in ③.

**Type and member check.** The hunk is +17/−1 inside the TSDoc block; `body?: any` (`:40`) is byte-identical; `rawBody`'s TSDoc (`:47-52`) is untouched; no other member, no export (`check:api-surface` sits inside the green `Lint & Repo Gates`; `Type Check · source gates` and the `TypeScript Type Check` aggregate are green). The dev's acceptance note on `rawBody`'s "consume the underlying request stream lazily" is right: JSON and form bodies were parsed before the handler before PR #24005 too, and the media types `body` does not read stay unread until `rawBody()`; the old text does not contradict the new one.

**Changeset sentences.** "What it is" restates S1 and S2 — right. "It may refuse" restates S3, S4 and S5, including "So a handler must not catch the refusal and carry on" — right, under the same MAY reading. "Raw bytes … reads `rawBody()` and never reads `body`" — right (S6; `rawBody` is a function, so the parentheses are exact). "Unchanged: the type (`body?: any`), every other member, and every runtime behaviour. This is prose in the shipped `.d.ts` only." — right against the diff.

**PR body.** Every pin the measured table names exists under that name in `request-body-refusal.test.ts` (checked one by one). "JSON is read with `text()`, which fills the same Hono body cache" is right (`request-body.ts:137-141`; hono's `json()` is `#cachedBody("text")` then `JSON.parse`).

### ② Semver level

`patch` for `@objectstack/spec` is right. The change is prose in the published `.d.ts`: `files[]` carries `dist`, `exports['./contracts']` resolves to `dist/contracts/index.d.ts` and `index.d.mts`, and the build's dts pass runs unless `OS_SKIP_DTS` is set (`package.json` `build`, `tsup.config.ts:324`). Nothing exported is added, removed or narrowed; no authorable key; no ADR-0087 id — so `Clause-②: no`, present on the changeset and on the PR body, is right and no disposition marker is owed. I did not rebuild (read-only); the dev's reported `dist` grep — the new sentence in both `.d.ts` files, the old sentence in neither, the untouched `rawBody` text as positive control — is consistent with that configuration. `Check Changeset` is green on this head; `check:api-surface`, `check:docs` and `check-changeset-fixed` sit inside the green `Lint & Repo Gates`.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Deviation 1, the trailer amend.** Accepted. The head commit carries the model-free pair and the session trailer; the amended tip was unpublished (an empty `git diff` against the gated tree, per the report), and the tree is what this record judges.
2. **Deviation 2, the worktree attached to an existing branch.** Accepted. The merge base is `e246f0611`, the base the claim named.
3. **Deviation 3, local narrowing.** Accepted. The four exit-3 families are prerequisite failures of a shallow clone or an unbuilt sibling, none reads the two changed files, and CI runs them; spec `pnpm test` was declared to `Test Core`, which is read in item 8.
4. **Deviation 4, no `subscribe_pr_activity`.** Not a review matter.
5. **Open question 1 (`{}` versus an absent `body`).** A is right. The card forbids a type change; the contract's own `Middleware` and fallback TSDoc already scope the `{}` sentence to the seams that populate `body`; the one producer that leaves it absent is a test fixture outside `dist` whose header says why; no real handler was shown to break on `undefined`. B is a type change for a card of its own, owed only on such a measurement. Residual stays as stated in S2.
6. **Open question 2 (the handler consequence).** A is right; the sentence states the measured shape (S4, S5) and invents no API.
7. **Out-of-scope finding, the conformance adapter.** A card, yes. `@objectstack/http-conformance` describes itself as "a zero-dependency node:http REFERENCE implementation of IHttpServer plus a cross-adapter suite" — the artefact a third-party adapter author copies, and the suite the contract itself names as what "locks cross-adapter behavior" (`http-server.ts`, the `write` member). Measured on `main`, its adapter diverges from the new contract on three counts, not the one the dev named: a malformed declared-JSON body becomes `{}` (`:387`); a `multipart/form-data` body with content becomes `{}` — not parsed, not refused (`isEagerlyParsed`, `:102-107`, `:381`), against S1; a `text/*` body becomes a string (`:391`), a value the contract never names. PR #24005's review accepted the first "for the private harness" while the contract said nothing; now the contract says what `body` is and the reference implementation does not deliver it (Prime Directive #10 on the reference, not on a product server). No conformance test drives `NodeHttpServer` with a malformed body — the only refusal suite (`hono-body-refusal.conformance.test.ts`) drives the two Hono doors — so the suite cannot pin the refusal for a third-party adapter either. Lane: the one that owned #23914 and #24005, `domain:cli` · `area:api`, grade for the triage seat (a validation instrument, no runtime path; p3 reads right). ⛔ Not this PR.
8. **Escalated to the seat, from S6: multipart `rawBody()` on the standard transport.** Derived from hono 4.13.12's cache code, not run: after the eager `parseBody()`, `rawBody()` returns a re-serialised form whose boundary does not match the request's `Content-Type` header, while the untouched `rawBody` TSDoc promises "binary uploads (file streams, multipart parts)". Pre-existing, unchanged by this diff, not pinned in either direction. No in-repo handler reads multipart wire bytes (the storage raw doors take the file's own media type), so this is a candidate card for the transport lane only after a measurement, not a finding against this PR.
9. **Wording residual, S6's "a file upload".** Non-blocking; "a raw upload (a PUT of the file's own media type)" would close it in a follow-up docs edit, or alongside item 7's card.
10. **Check-runs on `2a55ea381bfeda6b6b3cba3c7520c251a6222aa0`, read at 2026-10-16T23:18Z.** 40 runs, none failed. Success: `Build Core`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` (aggregate) with `Type Check · source gates`, `· workspace`, `· consumer gates` and `· debt ledger`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Spec property liveness`, every `Lint ·` sub-job, the four claim guards, `Auto Label`, the `Dogfood Regression Gate` aggregate, `filter`. Skipped by design: the dogfood matrix shards, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Temporal Conformance`, `Build Docs`, `Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke`. `Test Core (1/6)`, `(2/6)`, `(3/6)`, `(5/6)` and `(6/6)` are green; `Test Core (4/6)` was still in progress at that reading, so this record has NOT read that one shard; the diff is TSDoc plus a changeset, `Build Core` (the spec build the tests consume) is green, and the seat reads the shard before the queue. The Docs Drift Check comment is advisory and lists no page.
